generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and sport science, this approach shapes how you meet each practical, essay and exam. You take on a demanding topic like biomechanics or training physiology to understand it, trust that effort and practice will improve your work, and treat each task as a chance to grow, not just a grade. Across a module, those three habits become one way of studying.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students face the same coaching assignment. One sticks to a familiar drill to keep the mark safe, and decides tactics are simply not their strength. The other treats the task as a chance to improve, trusts that effort will pay off, and works to understand why each coaching choice matters. By the end, the second student understands the ideas and is more confident, because excelling, a growth mindset and learning motivation worked together.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and sport science, these three ideas work best together. You treat each practical, essay and exam as a chance to grow, trust that effort and practice will improve your work, and study to understand, not only to pass. That joined-up approach is what helps you start well and keep improving across your degree.

check.body: A student takes on a harder module topic to understand it better, believes they can improve with effort, and treats the work as a chance to grow rather than only a grade. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: The three ideas working as one approach: learning motivation, self-belief and excelling together.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three are at work in how this student approaches the task.
Choosing the harder topic to understand it is learning motivation, not performance motivation.
Believing they can improve with effort is a growth mindset, not a fixed one.
The student treats the work as a chance to grow, which is more than chasing marks.
